questions.stem:
Passage: The roots of sustainable development can be traced back to the 1972 Stockholm Conference, where development was for the first time linked to environment, emphasising the need for efforts at the international level. Sustainability is the ability of the earth's various systems including human cultural systems and economics, to survive and adapt to changing environmental conditions. Sustainable development implies a change in all aspects of life in a way that causes little damage to the environment. It is meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

The chief cause of unsustainability is the exponential growth of human population and overexploitation of natural resources. In developing countries, resource exploitation occurs chiefly to meet the needs of ever increasing human population for food, fuel, fodder and shelter. Various human activities like agriculture, deforestation, over-fishing, overuse of fresh water, etc. result in environmental degradation and social disintegration.

We have used technology to alter much of the rest of nature to meet our growing needs, like we have reduced biodiversity by destroying wildlife habitats. Some populations of pest species and disease causing bacteria have been strengthened through indiscriminate use of pesticides and antibiotics. Renewable resources have been used faster than they can be regenerated thus turning grasslands into deserts.

Sustainable development is further threatened by poverty, political instability, population growth, undernourishment and high consumption of natural resources. We need to act quickly to avoid disasters in the near future.

Question: Sustainable development implies:
options: a form of growth that does not meet the current human needs.
a form of development that overexploits natural resources.
a change in all aspects of life that causes little damage to the environment.
a form of growth that is meeting the needs of the present generation.
questions.explanation: The passage defines it as a change in all aspects of life that causes little damage to the environment.

questions.stem:
Passage: Planet, People, Profit: The 3Ps of the triple bottom line approach, which form the core of sustainable business operations, are more intertwined and inseparable today than they ever have been in the past. Natural calamities, global warming and governance issues are impacting reputations and businesses, along with heightened shareholder and consumer activism, and increased regulatory scrutiny. As a result, enterprises are compelled to take a hard look at the way they conduct their businesses and make sweeping changes in a bid to future-proof themselves.

An example of the way in which the landscape is changing can be found in the Indian banking system. The Reserve Bank of India recently proposed integrating climate-related risks into its practice of monitoring the stability of the financial system and modelling climate risk scenarios to identify vulnerabilities. This could imply that banks and financial institutions would need to chalk out new frameworks, imbibe climate change-related concerns into their credit decisions and risk management functions.

Globally, communities and corporations are re-evaluating priorities and redefining purpose at individual and collective levels. There has been a conscious crossover to a value addition approach, which goes beyond profits and pay cheques.

Champions of climate change, software engineers going back to their villages to start organic farming, start-up founders obsessed with leveraging technology to solve the problem of access to financial services, and teachers imparting education to underprivileged students are the real-life heroes of today. To them, 'why we do' matters as much as 'what we do'. Consequently, ESG (environmental awareness, social responsibility and good governance) have become the focal points of the lens through which governments, corporates and individuals are looking at their day-to-day jobs and decision-making.

Question: The central idea of the passage is:
options: change in the Indian banking system.
integrating climate-related risks with the financial system.
questions.explanation: The passage opens with the triple bottom line approach, the core of sustainable business operations, and builds on it.

It is trying to identify vulnerabilities of climate change related concerns.

questions.stem: Of the four given options, choose the most appropriate one.
options: His knowledge of Indian vernaculars are far superior to that of the common man.
His knowledge of Indian vernaculars is far superior to that of the common man.
His knowledges of Indian vernaculars are far superior to that of the common man.
His knowledge of Indian vernaculars has far superior to that of the common man's.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'knowledge' (singular, uncountable), so 'is' is correct.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which can replace the underlined word without changing the meaning of the sentence. The rapacious plunderers did not spare even the people living in the slums.
questions.explanation: Rapacious = greedy and grasping, so avaricious. (A candidate chose 'barbarous'.)

questions.stem: This question consists of a sentence divided into four parts numbered (1) to (4). Only one part is not acceptable in standard written English. Identify the part which contains an error. (1) We had in this village (2) a boy whom I well remember (3) whom from his childhood (4) showed a strong liking for bees.
options: a boy whom I well remember
showed a strong liking for bees.
questions.explanation: 'Whom' is wrong as the subject of 'showed'; it should be 'who'.

questions.stem: Of the four given options, choose the most appropriate one.
options: The news of his father's demise has broken him.
The news of his father's demise have broken him.
The news of his father's demise has broke him.
The news of his father's demise has been broken him.
questions.explanation: Singular subject 'news', present perfect 'has broken'.

questions.stem: Choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. an office for which no salary is paid
questions.explanation: An honorary post carries no pay. (A candidate chose 'gratis'.)

questions.stem: Of the four given options, choose the most appropriate one.
options: My sister is the poet and the philosopher.
My sister is a poet and philosopher.
My sister is a poet and the philosopher.
My sister is poet and philosopher.
questions.explanation: One article covers both nouns when they describe one person.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which can replace the underlined word without changing the meaning of the sentence. Arun was able to see the futility of his work after 20 years.
questions.explanation: Futility = uselessness, worthlessness.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which can replace the underlined word without changing the meaning of the sentence. The need of the hour is to initiate the renaissance of moral conscience and halt the rampant corruption for it could even hasten the end of our civilisation.
questions.explanation: Renaissance = revival or rebirth. (A candidate chose 'significance'.)

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: There is no glory in war ______ the blood it ______.
questions.explanation: 'Worth the blood it costs' is the natural idiom.

questions.stem:
Choose the most logical order of sentences from among the four choices to construct a coherent paragraph.
A. The man who is perpetually hesitating over which of the two things he will do first, will do neither.
B. He fluctuates from opinion to opinion and veers like a weather-cock.
C. Instead of being progressive in anything, he will be at best stationary and most probably regress in all.
D. It is only the man who first consults wisely, then resolves firmly, that can advance to eminence in any time.
questions.explanation: A states the problem, B describes the hesitating man, C his result, D contrasts the decisive man.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which is closest to the opposite in meaning of the underlined word in the sentence. You will have to conform to the rules if you want to stay here.
questions.explanation: Conform = obey; disobey is the opposite.

questions.stem:
Choose the most logical order of sentences from among the four choices to construct a coherent paragraph.
A. Nature seems to have taken particular care to disseminate her blessings among the different regions of the world.
B. Therefore, the natives of several parts of the globe have a kind of dependence upon one another.
C. The infusion of a china plant is sweetened by the pith of an Indian cane.
D. The food often grows in one country and sauce is prepared in another.
questions.explanation: A states the idea, D and C give examples, and B ('Therefore') concludes. (A candidate chose A, D, B, C.)

questions.stem:
Choose the most logical order of sentences from among the four choices to construct a coherent paragraph.
A. Such a place is called Oasis.
B. A great part of Arabia is desert.
C. The sand is so hot that you cannot walk over it with your bare feet in the day time.
D. However, springs of water here and there come up from under the ground that enable vegetation to grow.
questions.explanation: B introduces the desert, C describes it, D ('However') adds the springs, A names such a place. (A candidate chose C, D, B, A.)

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which is closest to the opposite in meaning of the underlined word in the sentence. Do not run after the momentary pleasures of this transient world.
questions.explanation: Transient = short-lived; permanent is the opposite. Brief, ephemeral and passing are synonyms.

questions.stem: Choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. a record of one's life written by somebody else
questions.explanation: A biography is written by someone else; an autobiography by oneself.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: Those who live in ______ houses should not throw ______ at others.
questions.explanation: Proverb: people in glass houses should not throw stones.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which is closest to the opposite in meaning of the underlined word in the sentence. We should not belittle others' achievements.
questions.explanation: Belittle = to make something seem unimportant. Praise is the closest opposite. 'Encourage' is also plausible, so treat the key with caution.

questions.stem: Of the four given options, choose the most appropriate one.
options: Neither of them were invited to the party.
Neither of them was invited to the party.
Neither of them invited to the party.
Neither of them have invited to the party.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' takes a singular verb. (A candidate chose option 3, which has no verb.)

questions.stem: Choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. that which is bound to happen
questions.explanation: Inevitable = certain to happen. (A candidate chose 'doubtful'.)

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: The relations between two friends are so ______ that no misunderstandings can ______ them.
questions.explanation: 'So strong that no misunderstandings can break them.'

questions.stem:
Choose the most logical order of sentences from among the four choices to construct a coherent paragraph.
A. Dog is known for its faithfulness.
B. It stands by humans in the time of prosperity and also in adversity.
C. It will sleep on the cold ground, if only it may be by the master's side.
D. And it will kiss the land that has no food to offer yet not betray its master.
questions.explanation: A states the claim, B generalises it, C and D give examples ('And' links D to C).

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: ______ politicians alone can survive in politics where ______ rules the roost.
questions.explanation: 'Wily politicians survive where treachery rules the roost.'

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks: He appears to be liberal in his views, but in actual life he is less ______ and is ______ narrow-minded than many others in the organisation.
questions.explanation: 'Less tolerant and more narrow-minded' fits the contrast.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which can replace the underlined word without changing the meaning of the sentence. He would have been successful, but for his lack of temerity.
questions.explanation: Temerity = reckless boldness, audacity. (A candidate chose 'confidence'.)

questions.stem: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase underlined in the sentence. The thief was caught red-handed and apprehended by the police.
options: with the hands smeared with blood
in the act of committing the crime
questions.explanation: Red-handed = in the very act.

questions.stem: This question consists of a sentence divided into four parts numbered (1) to (4). Only one part is not acceptable in standard written English. Identify the part which contains an error. (1) I had a partial father (2) who give me a better education (3) than his broken fortune (4) would have allowed.
options: who give me a better education
questions.explanation: 'Who give' should be 'who gave' (past tense). (A candidate chose part 3.)

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which can replace the underlined word without changing the meaning of the sentence. Most of the staff is restive under the new manager.
questions.explanation: Restive = restless and uneasy, discontented.

questions.stem: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase underlined in the sentence. What egged you on to become a social worker?
questions.explanation: To egg on = to urge or push. (A candidate chose 'inspired'.)

questions.stem: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase underlined in the sentence. It was he who put a spoke in my wheel.
options: helped in the execution of the plan
thwarted the execution of the plan
questions.explanation: To put a spoke in someone's wheel = to obstruct their plan.

questions.stem: Choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. allowance paid by a husband to his wife on legal separation
questions.explanation: Alimony is maintenance paid on separation or divorce.

questions.stem: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase underlined in the sentence. When he tells stories about himself he is inspired to draw the long bow.
questions.explanation: To draw the long bow = to exaggerate.

questions.stem: This question consists of a sentence divided into four parts numbered (1) to (4). Only one part is not acceptable in standard written English. Identify the part which contains an error. (1) This majestic mahogany table (2) which had one leg missing (3) belongs to an old prince (4) who is now impoverished.
questions.explanation: The tense clashes with the present 'belongs', so it should be 'which has one leg missing'. The key is not confirmed.

questions.stem: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase underlined in the sentence. My father strained every nerve to enable me to get settled in life.
options: spent a large amount of money
questions.explanation: To strain every nerve = to make a great effort. (A candidate chose 'tried all tricks'.)

questions.stem: This question consists of a sentence divided into four parts numbered (1) to (4). Only one part is not acceptable in standard written English. Identify the part which contains an error. (1) It is to be (2) the last expedition (3) before the school examinations, (4) which start on 12 December 2022.
questions.explanation: 'Which' refers to a single date or event in the writer's plan, so 'which starts' is expected. The key is not confirmed (the original may have another intended error).

questions.stem: Of the four given options, choose the most appropriate one.
options: No sooner had he returned than he left again.
No sooner he had returned than he left again.
No sooner had he returned but he left again.
No sooner had he returned when he left again.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' needs inversion and is followed by 'than'. (A candidate chose option 2.)

questions.stem: Choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. a person who is always dissatisfied
questions.explanation: A malcontent is a habitually dissatisfied person. (A candidate chose 'avaricious'.)

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which is closest to the opposite in meaning of the underlined word in the sentence. Quite a few of the listeners complained that the speaker's speech was not comprehensible.
questions.explanation: The underlined word is 'incomprehensible' in sense; the closest opposite among the options that describes unclear speech is 'unclear'. The original item looks flawed, so treat with caution.

questions.stem: This question consists of a sentence divided into four parts numbered (1) to (4). Only one part is not acceptable in standard written English. Identify the part which contains an error. (1) Shifts in regional climate (2) will also impact (3) national parks, wild reserves (4) and mountain tops with high altitude.
options: and mountain tops with high altitude.
questions.explanation: The natural phrasing is 'high altitude mountain tops'.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which is closest to the opposite in meaning of the underlined word in the sentence. The Chairman initiated the proceedings with a brief speech.
questions.explanation: Initiated = began; concluded is the opposite. (A candidate chose 'confused'.)

questions.stem: Azp, Cxq, Evr, Gus, Irt, Kou. The wrong term in the above series is:
questions.explanation: First letters go up by 2, second letters go down by 2 (z, x, v, t, r, p), third letters go up by 1. So Gus should be Gtp's pattern term 'Gts'.

questions.stem: If 'DRINK' is coded as 'WIRMP', then 'SMOKE' is coded as:
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (27 - position): D-W, R-I, I-R, N-M, K-P. So S-H, M-N, O-L, K-P, E-V gives HNLPV.

questions.stem: If 12th July falls 3 days after tomorrow which is Tuesday, then what day of the week will fall on the last day of the month?
questions.explanation: Tomorrow is Tuesday, so 12 July is Friday. 31 July is 19 days later; 19 mod 7 = 5, and Friday + 5 = Wednesday.

questions.stem: P, Q and R invested in business in the ratio of 5:6:8, respectively. After one year, R withdrew 50% of his investment, and P invested an additional 60% of his investment. After 2 years, what is the ratio of distribution of profit among them, respectively?
questions.explanation: Capital x time: P = 5 x 1 + 8 x 1 = 13; Q = 6 x 2 = 12; R = 8 x 1 + 4 x 1 = 12. So 13 : 12 : 12. (A candidate chose 14:12:11.)

questions.stem: How many times does the digit 6 appear between 501 and 599?
questions.explanation: Units place: 506, 516, ..., 596 = 10. Tens place: 560-569 = 10. Total 20 appearances.

questions.stem: Find the ratio at which salt of Rs 17.00 per kg should be mixed with salt of Rs 20.00 per kg to produce salt of Rs 18.40 per kg.
A cyclist rides 12 km to the East, turns North and rides 8 km, turns left and rides 6 km. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: After turning left from North he faces West. Net position = (12 - 6, 8) = (6, 8), so distance = 10 km.

questions.stem: Accident : Carefulness :: Disease : ?
questions.explanation: Carefulness prevents accidents; sanitation prevents disease. (A candidate chose 'Doctor'.)

questions.stem: By how much above the cost price should the goods be marked for sale so that after allowing a trade discount of 20% and a cash discount of 12.5%, a net gain of 40% on the cost price is made?
questions.explanation: Let CP = 100. Final price 140; before the 12.5% cash discount = 160; before the 20% trade discount = 200. So 100% above CP. (Option 3 was garbled in the scan.)

questions.stem: A sum of money yields compound interest of Rs 720.00 in one year and Rs 1483.20 in two years, compounded annually. What is the rate of interest?
questions.explanation: Second-year interest = 1483.20 - 720 = 763.20. The extra 43.20 over 720 is interest on 720, so r = 43.2/720 = 6%.

questions.stem: If A @ B means A is the mother of B, A $ B means A is the father of B, A # B means A is the sister of B, A * B means A is the brother of B, then M $ N * O # P does NOT mean:
options: O is the daughter of M
N, O, P are children of M
O is the sister of N and P
P is the brother of M
questions.explanation: M is the father of N; N is the brother of O; O is the sister of P. So P is M's child, not M's brother.

questions.stem: If A @ B means A is the mother of B, A $ B means A is the father of B, A # B means A is the sister of B, A * B means A is the brother of B, then A * B @ C # D means:
options: A is the uncle of C
C is the brother of A
D is the daughter of A
questions.explanation: A is the brother of B; B is the mother of C; so A is C's maternal uncle.

questions.stem: A 100 m long train is running at a speed of 72 km/hr. How much time will it take to cross a bridge 240 m long?
questions.explanation: 72 km/h = 20 m/s. Distance = 100 + 240 = 340 m, so time = 17 s. (A candidate chose 16 s.)

questions.stem: Pointing to a lady, Saurabh said "She is the daughter of the woman who is the mother of the husband of my mother". How is the lady related to Saurabh?
questions.explanation: The husband of Saurabh's mother is his father; the father's mother is his paternal grandmother; her daughter is his paternal aunt.

questions.stem: Garima is older than her cousin Mamta. Mamta's brother Brahm is older than Garima. When Mamta and Brahm visit Garima, all three like to play together. Mamta wins more often than Garima does. Which of the following is true from above?
options: Brahm wins more often than Mamta
Garima is the oldest of the three
Mamta is the youngest of the three
questions.explanation: Age order: Brahm > Garima > Mamta, so Mamta is the youngest. Nothing is stated about Brahm's winning record.

questions.stem: Divide Rs 4200 between Aditya and Aradhika so that the amount received by Aditya at the end of 4 years is equal to the amount received by Aradhika at the end of 5 years; compound interest being at 10% per annum, compounded annually.
Seema's salary was reduced by 60%. Subsequently, the reduced salary was increased by 60%. Find her loss in terms of percentage.
questions.explanation: 0.4 x 1.6 = 0.64 of the original, a 36% loss.

questions.stem:
P, Q, R, S, T and U are students of a college. Q and R are good at both Biology and Chemistry. T and R are good at both Computers and Maths. U is good at Chemistry only. S is good at all subjects, except Physics and Maths. P and Q are good at both Physics and Maths. There are five subjects Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Maths and Computers.

Question: Who is good at all subjects, except Computers?
questions.explanation: Q: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Maths. R lacks Physics; S lacks Physics and Maths.

questions.stem:
P, Q, R, S, T and U are students of a college. Q and R are good at both Biology and Chemistry. T and R are good at both Computers and Maths. U is good at Chemistry only. S is good at all subjects, except Physics and Maths. P and Q are good at both Physics and Maths. There are five subjects Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Maths and Computers.

Question: Who are good at two subjects only?
questions.explanation: P: Physics and Maths. T: Computers and Maths. (A candidate chose 'S and P', but S has three subjects.)

questions.stem:
P, Q, R, S, T and U are students of a college. Q and R are good at both Biology and Chemistry. T and R are good at both Computers and Maths. U is good at Chemistry only. S is good at all subjects, except Physics and Maths. P and Q are good at both Physics and Maths. There are five subjects Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Maths and Computers.

Question: Who is good only at Maths and Computers?
questions.explanation: T is good at Computers and Maths only.

questions.stem: Among the six schools of Indian Philosophy, who established the 'Vaisheshika' system?
questions.explanation: Vaisheshika was founded by Kanada. Gotama founded Nyaya; Jaimini, Mimamsa.

questions.stem: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757. The name Plassey is derived from:
options: Palash tree known for its beautiful flowers
questions.explanation: Plassey comes from 'Palashi', after the palash (flame of the forest) trees. (The paper's '1756' is a misprint; the battle was in 1757.)

questions.stem: Which one of the following objectives of the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) is incorrect?
options: Extends funding to micro-units and entrepreneurs.
It extended funding support for activities allied to agriculture also.
It has launched three innovative products namely Shishu, Kishore and Tarun.
It extends funding support to the corporate small business sector up to Rs 50 Lakh.
questions.explanation: Mudra loans go to non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises, up to Rs 10 lakh (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun).

questions.stem: 'Mahal' in Mahalwari revenue settlement meant:
questions.explanation: In the Mahalwari system the 'mahal' was a village or group of villages.

questions.stem: Which among the following is NOT correctly matched?
options: Birth rate: The number of live births per 1000 population per year
Death rate: The number of deaths per 1000 population per year
Infant mortality rate: The number of deaths of babies before the age of five years per 1000 live birth
Natural decrease: When death rates are higher than birth rates (expressed as percentage)
questions.explanation: The infant mortality rate counts deaths before age one, not five.

questions.stem: The empirical climate classification scheme was developed by:
questions.explanation: Wladimir Koeppen developed the empirical climate classification.

questions.stem: Which among the following is NOT correct for geothermal energy?
options: Geothermal plants occupy relatively small land areas
It has extremely low environmental impact
It is dependent on weather conditions (like wind and solar power)
questions.explanation: Geothermal energy comes from heat inside the earth and does not depend on weather. (A candidate chose option 4.)

questions.stem: Which Constitution Amendment Act restored the power of the State Governments to identify and specify Socially and Economically Backward Classes?
options: The Constitution (One Hundred and Fourth Amendment) Act, 2019
The Constitution (One Hundred and Fifth Amendment) Act, 2021
The Constitution (One Hundred and Second Amendment) Act, 2018
The Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016
questions.explanation: The 105th Amendment (2021) restored states' power to maintain their own OBC lists after the Maratha quota judgment. (A candidate chose the 104th.)

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the International Monetary Fund (IMF): (i) The Board of Governors is the highest decision-making body of the IMF. (ii) Its resources mainly come from the money that countries pay as their capital subscription (quotas) when they become members. How many of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT included in the 'Geneva Package' of the Twelfth Ministerial Conference (MC12) of the WTO?
options: Relaxing patent regulations for global vaccine equity
Agreement on subsidies to the fisheries sector
questions.explanation: The package covered vaccines (TRIPS decision), food security, fisheries subsidies and e-commerce. An ecological balance item was not part of it.

questions.stem: The motion of the moon around the earth is due to the:
questions.explanation: Gravity provides the centripetal force.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a Non-Government Organization dedicated to wildlife conservation?
questions.explanation: The Indian Board for Wildlife is a government advisory body.

questions.stem: Which Constitution Amendment Act ceased the reservation of seats for Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies?
options: The Constitution (One Hundred and Third Amendment) Act
The Constitution (One Hundred and Fourth Amendment) Act
The Constitution (One Hundred and Fifth Amendment) Act
The Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act
questions.explanation: The 104th Amendment (2019) ended Anglo-Indian nominations and extended SC/ST reservation to 2030.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true about Ultrasound waves?
options: Ultrasound waves are low frequency waves.
Ultrasound waves are generally used to clean parts located in hard-to-reach places.
Ultrasound scanners get images of internal organs of the human body.
Ultrasound waves can be used to detect cracks and flaws in metal blocks.
questions.explanation: Ultrasound has frequencies above 20,000 Hz, which is high frequency. (A candidate chose option 4.)

questions.stem: ______ is a black, thick liquid with unpleasant smell. It is a mixture of about 200 substances and products obtained from it are used in synthetic dyes, drugs, perfumes, explosives, paints etc.
questions.explanation: This describes coal tar.

questions.stem: ______ captures digital information of peoples' lives from various sources that public and private entities use to influence behaviour.
questions.explanation: The Internet of Behaviour (IoB) uses collected data to influence behaviour.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Peninsular rivers in India?
options: Smaller, fixed course with well-adjusted valleys
questions.explanation: Peninsular rivers are old and mature, not young and youthful. (A candidate chose option 4.)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding the Scheme for Adolescent Girls (SAG)?
options: The Anganwadi Centre is the focal point for the delivery of the services.
The scheme focuses on two major components - nutrition and non-nutrition.
The scheme also aims at mainstreaming out-of-school girls to school system.
questions.explanation: The scheme grew out of the earlier Sabla programme and was not introduced in 2020. Treat this key with some caution.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT correct about WTO?
options: It sets the rules for global trade.
It is a successor to The General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs (GATT).
questions.explanation: The WTO has 164 members (as of 2022). (A candidate chose option 2.)

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT correct about the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)?
options: It came into being to implement US President Dwight Eisenhower's 'Atoms for Peace' proposal.
It seeks to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy.
It has no right to inspect civilian nuclear facilities of a sovereign state.
questions.explanation: The IAEA inspects civilian nuclear facilities under safeguards agreements.

questions.stem: 'Blossom Shower' enables the flowering of:
questions.explanation: Blossom showers (pre-monsoon rain) trigger coffee flowering in Karnataka and Kerala.

questions.stem: The Rigveda includes hymns called 'Sukta'. What does 'Sukta' mean?
questions.explanation: Sukta = 'well said' (su + ukta). (A candidate chose 'true statement'.)

questions.stem: Whose speech, delivered at the Parliament of the World's Religions in 1893, began with the words 'Sisters and brothers of America...'?
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda's Chicago address.

questions.stem: The 'Great Leap Forward' campaign was initiated in 1958 in ______ aiming at industrialising the country on a massive scale.
questions.explanation: Mao Zedong launched the Great Leap Forward in China.

questions.stem: Which of the following options is NOT available in the Drawing group, under the Home tab in MS-PowerPoint?
questions.explanation: Line spacing is in the Paragraph group.

questions.stem: Physical parts of a computer are called ______ of the computer system.
questions.explanation: Physical components are hardware.

questions.stem: Unauthorized access to a bank account for carrying online transactions is an example of ______.
questions.explanation: Unauthorised access is hacking. (A candidate chose 'Intellectual property theft'.)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct? a) Cache memory is used for storing data and instructions used during program execution. b) Program and data files not required immediately by the computer system are stored on the hard disk. c) Program and data files rarely required are stored in RAM.
questions.explanation: Rarely used files are kept on secondary storage, not RAM, so (c) is false.

questions.stem: The arrangement of computers and other peripherals in a network is called its ______.
questions.explanation: Topology describes the layout of a network.

questions.stem: The ______ interprets and carries out the basic instructions that operate the computer.
questions.explanation: The CPU executes instructions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect for a Word document?
options: It cannot be converted to a portable document format.
It can be shared online with collaborators.
It can be published as a web document.
It can be posted as a blog.
questions.explanation: Word documents can be saved or exported as PDF. (A candidate chose option 3.)

questions.stem: A ______ is a set of rules that governs the communication between computers on a network.
questions.explanation: A protocol is a set of communication rules. (A candidate chose 'Server'.)

questions.stem: In order to change the character spacing of text in MS-PowerPoint, which of the following is used?
questions.explanation: Character Spacing is in the Font group. (A candidate chose 'Editing group'.)

questions.stem: NIC stands for:
questions.explanation: NIC = Network Interface Card. (A candidate chose option 4.)

questions.stem: An email received by a receiver consists of an attachment. When he opens the attachment, it results in the message being resent to everyone in the Microsoft Outlook address book of the receiver. What might be the contents of the attachment?
questions.explanation: Self-replicating mail-spreading code is a virus or worm.

questions.stem: Which of the following provides information about the current state of what you are viewing in the window in an MS Word document?
questions.explanation: The status bar shows page, word count, zoom and other state. (A candidate chose 'Scroll Bar'.)

questions.stem: Selected text in a word document appears ______ on the screen.
questions.explanation: Selected text is shown highlighted. (A candidate chose 'Subscripted'.)

questions.stem: Which of the following devices is NOT an input device?
questions.explanation: A printer outputs information.

questions.stem: Which one of the following options lists all secondary storage devices?
questions.explanation: Hard disk, pendrive and CD-ROM are all secondary (permanent) storage.

questions.stem: Among the storage devices, ______ is faster than ______.
questions.explanation: A hard disk is faster than a compact disk. (A candidate chose option 3.)

questions.stem: HTTP is the acronym for:
questions.explanation: HTTP = Hyper Text Transfer Protocol.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true?
options: Hacking a computer is always illegal and punishable by law.
Cookies allow a visited website to store its own information about a user on the user's computer
Open source software is computer software with its source code made available
A firewall is a program or hardware device that filters the information coming through an internet connection to a computer system
questions.explanation: Ethical hacking with permission is legal.

questions.stem: Which one of the following options is an incorrect way of clearing the contents of cells in an Excel worksheet?
options: Select row - Right click - Clear contents
Select column - Right click - Clear contents
questions.explanation: There is no Cells group with Clear on the Data tab. (A candidate chose option 3.)

questions.stem: ______ utility helps to find and format the cells that match the given criteria in an Excel worksheet.
questions.explanation: Conditional formatting highlights cells that meet criteria.

questions.stem: In a given criteria, ______ utility hides the cells that do not satisfy the condition:
questions.explanation: A data filter hides rows that do not match.

questions.stem: Which of the following should be strictly avoided to keep your computer system secure?
options: Turning on the option to automatically download and install the updates of the antivirus software
questions.explanation: Never share passwords.

questions.stem: MS-Word provides some pre-defined category-wise basic images that can be used directly by choosing the ______ option.
questions.explanation: Clip Art gives ready-made images. (A candidate chose 'Word Art'.)

questions.stem: A ______ is a program or hardware that filters the information coming through an internet connection to a network or a computer system.
questions.explanation: A firewall filters traffic. (A candidate chose 'Cookies'.)
